issues.detail: The Greek 'εδοθη αυτω' (edothē autō) means 'it was given TO him' (the angel), but the Vietnamese 'nó được ban cho quyền' translates it as 'it was given [to him] the power/right', which slightly shifts the focus. More importantly, the Greek 'καυματισαι' is an infinitive of purpose or result ('to burn'), whereas the Vietnamese 'quyền làm sém' adds the concept of 'power/right' (quyền) which is not explicitly in the Greek text.
